findings.description: [AI-SAST via Code Scan Verification Validation | claude-opus-5] Access-token handling in this file is clean (JWT issuance centralised in jwt_tokens.encode_token, token values never logged, token_version excluded from UPDATABLE_PROFILE_FIELDS, invalidate_issued_tokens on every password change), but two parts of this CM cannot be settled from this file alone: send_code_to_phone_number prints a password-reset code in cleartext to stdout at line 221, and the transport requirement (tokens in headers/body rather than query parameters) plus the access-logging requirement are implemented in route and middleware modules outside this CM's modified-file set | verdict=partial confidence=low

findings_aggregated_for_sde.desc: [AI-SAST via Code Scan Verification Validation | claude-opus-5] app/apis/auth/utils/utils.py: access-token handling in this file is clean - JWT issuance is centralised in jwt_tokens.encode_token so the signing algorithm cannot drift, token values are never written to a log, token_version is excluded from UPDATABLE_PROFILE_FIELDS so a client cannot write it, and invalidate_issued_tokens revokes outstanding tokens on every password change. Two parts of this CM cannot be settled from this file alone: send_code_to_phone_number (line 221) prints a password-reset code in cleartext to stdout, and the transport requirement (tokens in headers/body rather than query parameters) plus the access-logging requirement are implemented in route and middleware modules outside this CM's modified-file set. Partial coverage, not a cited vulnerability. | verdict=partial confidence=low
